la:noun:nympha.html:
nympha, ae, and nymphē, ēs (
dat. plur. NYMPHABVS, ; NYMFABVS,; NYMPHIS,; sq.), f., = νύμφη.
A bride, a mistress, ; (al. merita).—
A young woman: se quoque nympha tuis ornavit Iardanis armis,.—
Nymphae, demi-goddesses, who inhabit the sea, rivers, fountains, woods, trees, and mountains; nymphs: Nymphae, genus amnibus unde est,; ; : Nympha Maenalis,i. e. Carmenta, the mother of Evander,: Nymphae Libethrides,the Muses,: vocalis Nymphe,Echo,. Vows were made to the fountain-nymphs in cases of sickness or of drought, ; —
Transf., water (poet.): et cadit in patulos Nympha Aniena lacus, (4, 15), 4.—
A fountain, .—
The pupa or nymph of an insect: alius evolat, alius in nymphā est, alius in vermiculo,; .

Nymphaeum, i, n., = Νύμφαιον,
a promontory and seaport in Illyria, on the borders of Macedonia, now Capo di Redeni, ; ; ; .
